era_setting.place: Three Mile Island Unit 2 on an island in the Susquehanna River near Middletown, Pennsylvania -- its control room, its auxiliary building, its cooling towers -- and a federal courtroom in Harrisburg
era_setting.notes: The accident is 28 March 1979 and the criminal case runs to February 1984. This is the late 1970s and early 1980s in central Pennsylvania: analogue instrumentation, rows of backlit annunciator tiles, strip-chart recorders, rotary telephones, a line-printer on continuous fanfold paper, CRT terminals with green text, 1979 cars, brown and orange interiors. NOTHING digital-modern: no flat panels, no mobile phones, no LED, no modern signage. The courtroom material is 1983-84. The cooling towers are hyperboloid concrete and they emit WATER VAPOUR, never smoke.

forbidden_subjects: black smoke from a cooling tower
radiation warning sign close enough to read
recognisable face of a real individual
forbidden_claims: That anybody died at Three Mile Island, or that the accident is known to have caused cancer or any physical illness. The Commission found no detectable additional cases would result (ledger TM-703) -- AND that finding may never appear without its own caveat, that the health effects of a few rems or less are not known (TM-704). The two rows travel together, always.

That the falsified leak-rate tests caused the accident. The count Met-Ed pleaded guilty to covers conduct ending ON the morning of 28 March 1979 (TM-203). No source in the ledger connects the falsification to the accident sequence. The film may say the test that should have caught a leak had been meaningless for months; it may not say it caused the meltdown.

That Met-Ed was convicted of falsifying records under the federal false-statements law. The one Title 18 count -- Count 11 -- was DISMISSED (TM-205, TM-303, TM-305). The conviction is on Count 2, under the Atomic Energy Act and 10 C.F.R. Part 50 Appendix B.

That the fine was a million dollars. The fine was $45,000 (TM-304). The $1,000,000 was a condition of the plea agreement, paid to the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency for emergency planning within 20 miles (TM-311). 'To clean up the plant' is false.

That an individual operator was convicted over the accident. One former supervisor was convicted in a SEPARATE case for submitting another person's examination work as his own (TM-321). That is not the accident and he is never named.

That the operators were incompetent, or that they are the villains. The Commission found each 'was a product of his training -- training that did not adequately prepare them' (TM-415), that the fundamental problems were people-related rather than equipment (TM-603), and that an accident like this was eventually inevitable (TM-607).
The 3,300 person-rem collective dose. It does not appear in Kemeny, Rogovin or NUREG-0660 (TM-702). The figure is 2,000 person-rems, cited to Kemeny p.34.
Any reactor-order or cancellation statistic. None exists in the ledger's corpus (TM-807). The 'the industry stopped' beat is carried by Kemeny p.13 on public confidence (TM-806).
That a general evacuation was ordered. It was an ADVISORY, from the Governor, to pregnant women and preschool children, within 5 miles, from 30 March to 9 April (TM-709).

Any figure not in the facts ledger, and in particular the two OCR-corrupted numbers flagged there: the high-pressure-injection throttle-back interval (TM-409) and the alarm printer's lag (TM-505). Both are quoted in the ledger with a warning; neither may go on screen until confirmed on the page image.

beats.headline: 4:00:36 A.M.
beats.notes: The first pump trip. Held silent.

beats.headline: THIRTEEN SECONDS
beats.notes: When the valve should have closed.

beats.headline: WHERE THE WATER GOES
beats.notes: Coolant loop drawn as a mechanism. No lettering.

beats.headline: 1,000 A MINUTE / UNDER 100
beats.notes: High-pressure injection started, then was throttled. The INTERVAL is OCR-corrupted (TM-409) and must not appear -- only the two flow figures, which are verbatim.

beats.headline: IT WASN'T GIVING US ANY USEFUL INFORMATION
beats.notes: An operator, to the Commission. Verbatim, designed typography, never a facsimile.

beats.headline: A YELLOW MAINTENANCE TAG
beats.notes: Illustrate a tag hanging over an indicator light. No legible text.

beats.headline: OCTOBER 1978 TO 28 MARCH 1979
beats.notes: The charged period. It ENDS on the morning of the accident -- the card must not imply causation.

beats.headline: WHAT THE COUNTS SAID
beats.notes: One guilty, six no contest, four dismissed -- including the only Title 18 count. Built one line at a time.
The fine, and the payment that was not a fine. The card must label which is which.

beats.headline: 2,000 PERSON-REMS
beats.notes: Against 240,000 of annual background for the same population.

beats.headline: EVENTUALLY INEVITABLE
beats.notes: The Commission's own last word. Verbatim.

notes: EP84 of the EP83-85 slate (owner GO 2026-08-25). Bands as EP83: 29-35 minutes on the slate's AVP basis, word band divided at the rate this register actually delivers (EP77-82 measured 184-202 raw wpm, not the 171.79 registry model). Size with gen_narration_case --dry-run and confirm with --measure-section before writing to length. era_setting is unusually strict because the single most likely visual failure here is a 2020s control room: this plant's instrumentation is the story, and a flat panel in frame destroys it. The cooling towers emit water vapour -- a plate showing smoke would be a factual error the audience will catch instantly.
